plan.strategy: Measure the provided seed implementation unchanged to establish the baseline latency and correctness for torch.fix truncation
plan.code_changes: None; seed written verbatim to tmp/main.py
plan.hypothesis: The seed's floor/ceil + sign-bit restoration kernel preserves -0/NaN/Inf semantics and passes all 18 correctness cases; baseline geo_mean establishes the reference ratio

conclusion.root_cause: Seed baseline passes all 18 correctness cases bit-exactly (abs_err=0, matched_ratio=1) but is slow: geo_mean 0.518. Two independent gaps, both measured: (1) per-call host cost is ~26 us versus ~14 us for the reference torch.fix on every workload with n<=1M (9 of 12 timing cases sit at a flat 0.67-0.74x regardless of size, so the difference is host submit, not device work); (2) at n=16.7M the device kernel costs ~127 us of the ~152 us latency while the reference executes the same case inside its ~19.8 us host floor, and fp16 (0.13x) and fp32 (0.13x/0.59x) cost nearly the same despite 2x different byte counts, which points to vector-instruction count and per-block overhead rather than DMA bandwidth. The seed's kernel also masks every load/store even when BLOCK divides n exactly, and spends 9 vector ops per element (cvt, cmp, floor, ceil, select, 2x and, or, cvt).
conclusion.perf_gap_analysis: No previous measurement to compare against (first round). Workload-level facts recorded for the next round: flat ~0.69x for n in {1024, 65536, 1048576} across fp16/bf16/fp32, 0.1298x for fp16 4096x4096, 0.1287x for bf16 4096x4096, 0.5876x for fp32 4096x4096; min_speedup 0.1287 at fix-timing-7.
conclusion.next_suggestion: Remove the per-element mask on the contiguous path when BLOCK divides n, raise the tile to 8192 elements, replace floor+ceil+select (9 vector ops) with an abs/floor/sign-restore form (6 vector ops), and slim the host path (drop memory_format on the fast path, cache the raw-stream getter and device index) to attack both the flat host-bound cases and the op-count-bound 16.7M cases.
conclusion.debug_lesson: Target-side probing showed torch.empty_like ~5.6 us and the raw Triton launcher dominating the remaining host cost; because eval timing is submit-limited for all n<=1M, device-side tuning cannot move those cases.
conclusion.strategy_evolution: Baseline measured; next round attacks mask removal, tile size, vector-op count and host glue together, then a final round tunes based on per-case evidence.

plan.strategy: Establish measured baseline with the provided seed Triton trunc kernel (nomask/masked/strided paths, one tile per program, cached launch metadata)
plan.code_changes: None; seed written verbatim as tmp/main.py
plan.hypothesis: Seed reproduces the recorded 0.789 score; large 4096x4096 fp16/bf16 workloads are the main deficit (~0.30 speedup) due to 2048 tiny programs

expected_effect.mechanism: Measure unmodified seed to anchor all later comparisons

conclusion.root_cause: Seed kernel launches one BLOCK-sized tile per program, so 4096x4096 (16.7M elements) creates 2048 tiny programs on a 20-core device; each program does a serialized load->vector->store with no cross-tile pipelining, achieving only ~0.84 TB/s effective HBM traffic (fp16) vs ~1.35 TB/s for the CANN reference. Small shapes are already host-overhead bound and slightly faster than reference (1.10-1.19x).
conclusion.perf_gap_analysis: Baseline established: geo_mean 0.9048 over 12 timing workloads. Deficits are concentrated in the three 16.7M-element shapes: fix-timing-3 (fp16) 0.313, fix-timing-7 (bf16) 0.322, fix-timing-11 (fp32) 0.820. All other nine workloads are 1.10-1.19x. Lifting the three large shapes to ~0.9 alone would move geo_mean to roughly 1.08, so large-shape DMA organization is the only lever that matters.
conclusion.next_suggestion: Replace the one-tile-per-program launch for large contiguous inputs with a multi-tile persistent kernel: small fixed program count (capped by tl.num_programs stride), each program loops over many BLOCK tiles so the compiler can pipeline load/compute/store across iterations. Microbenchmark grid x BLOCK x num_stages on the target before the next formal round.
conclusion.strategy_evolution: Seed established as baseline; next step targets per-program DMA pipelining for large shapes.

plan.strategy: Replace one-tile-per-program launches for large contiguous inputs with a persistent multi-tile kernel whose program count is the device vector-core count
plan.code_changes: Added _fix_loop / _fix_loop_tail persistent kernels (compile-time TILES/N, stride by tl.num_programs(0), num_stages=2). For n >= 8*8192 the launch uses grid = min(tiles, vector_core_num from torch.npu.get_device_properties, task-derived fallback) with BLOCK=8192 instead of one program per 8192-element tile. Small/odd shapes keep the previous one-tile-per-program paths; strided path unchanged. Launch metadata still warmed once and reused via raw launch.
plan.hypothesis: The three 4096x4096 workloads are limited by 2048 tiny single-tile programs (one serialized load->vector->store each). A persistent kernel with one program per vector core (40 on the probe device), each looping over ~51 tiles, lets the compiler pipeline the tiles and raises effective bandwidth, so fp16/bf16 speedups should roughly double and fp32 should improve slightly.

expected_effect.mechanism: Each program streams many tiles so load/compute/store pipeline across iterations instead of paying per-program dispatch and an unoverlapped single-tile DMA; measured device time for the 4096x4096 fp16 case drops from ~80us to ~34us

conclusion.root_cause: The persistent entries were built with kern.warmup(..., num_stages=2), which did not yield a usable compiled launch, so entry.launch stayed None and every call used the slow JIT dispatch path (~100us of Python per call, size independent). Additionally the threshold n>=65536 routed medium shapes (65536..1M elements, device time only a few microseconds) onto the loop path, where that fixed host cost dominated.
conclusion.perf_gap_analysis: Expected a large gain on the three 4096x4096 shapes; observed a global regression from geo_mean 0.9048 to 0.4456. Nine of twelve timing workloads moved to ~80-88us regardless of size (e.g. fix-timing-6, 1M bf16: 21.9->87.7us; fix-timing-1: 23.3->81.8us), while fix-timing-3 (fp16 16.7M) stayed flat at 80.6us and fix-timing-11 (fp32 16.7M) improved 116.6->88.7us. A size-independent ~80us floor indicates per-call host cost, not device time: the loop entry never obtained the cached raw launch (warmup with a launch-level num_stages argument failed), so every call fell through to full Triton JIT dispatch. Probe measurement of the same kernel shape put its real device time at only ~33.5us (fp16) and ~97us (fp32), confirming the device side did improve while the host path regressed.
conclusion.next_suggestion: Re-submit the persistent kernel but move loop pipelining from the launch option into tl.range(num_stages=2) inside the kernel body, warm up with the proven plain call (no num_stages kwarg) so the cached raw launch is built, and only take the persistent path when that raw launch is actually available (otherwise fall back to the seed one-tile kernel). That keeps the 33.5us device win without risking the JIT-dispatch regression.
conclusion.debug_lesson: Three probes and one eval established the mechanism: (1) the persistent loop kernel's *device* time is genuinely better (reps-slope K=33.5us fp16 16.7M vs ~80us for one-tile-per-program; probe5: constexpr vs runtime TILES identical, 33.5 vs 31.3); (2) the eval regression came from launch metadata: probe6 showed raw_launch=False for loop-path entries, so every call paid full Triton JIT dispatch (cand.run 175us vs torch.fix 80us per call in the debug harness); (3) a constexpr-vs-runtime TILES change is not a factor, so the failed warmup(..., num_stages=2) call is the suspect. Lesson: verify that the cached raw launch actually exists before assuming a kernel-structure win translates to end-to-end time.
conclusion.strategy_evolution: Architecture is right but the host launch path must be preserved: keep the persistent multi-tile kernel, move pipelining into the kernel body, and make the persistent path conditional on a successful cached raw launch with the seed kernel as fallback.

plan.strategy: Keep the persistent multi-tile kernel but guarantee its host launch path: pipelining inside the kernel body, plain warmup, and fall back to the seed kernel if no cached raw launch is obtained
plan.code_changes: Moved loop pipelining from the launch option into the kernel body (tl.range(..., num_stages=2)) and warm up the persistent kernel with the plain, already-proven call (no num_stages kwarg) so the cached raw launch is actually built. Added a plain-range kernel variant as a build-time fallback. The persistent entry is now only used when compiled.run.launch is available; otherwise the one-tile-per-program kernel is used for that shape.
plan.hypothesis: Round 2's regression was caused purely by the lost raw launch (JIT dispatch per call), not by the kernel. With pipelining baked into tl.range and a plain warmup, the persistent kernel should keep its ~33.5us device time (fp16 16.7M) end to end, lifting fix-timing-3/-7 from 0.31 to about 0.7, while medium and small shapes stay on their previous (~22us host-bound) behaviour thanks to the fallback.

expected_effect.mechanism: Same persistent kernel now runs through the cached low-level launch (~20us host) instead of Triton JIT dispatch (~100us host), so the measured 33.5us device time for fp16 16.7M is no longer masked

key_params.fallback: one-tile kernel when no raw launch

conclusion.root_cause: The cached low-level launcher call copied from the seed kernel passes 9 fixed slots plus 3 values (X, Y, BLOCK) for a 3-formal kernel. The persistent kernel has 4 formals (X, Y, TILES, BLOCK), so the launcher needs 13 arguments; the 12-argument call raised TypeError, which the fallback silently converted into permanent JIT dispatch for that shape.
conclusion.perf_gap_analysis: Expected the persistent kernel to reach about 0.7 on the fp16/bf16 4096x4096 shapes; observed all nine loop-path workloads pinned at 85-88us with geo_mean 0.4268. The measured pattern matches max(host, device) with a constant ~85us host cost: fix-timing-11 (fp32 16.7M, device ~97-106us) is unaffected at 106.3us (speedup 1.008, better than round 1's 116.6us), while fp16 16.7M (device ~33.5us) still costs 85.2us. So the device improvement is real but the host path is still Triton JIT dispatch: the cached raw launch was obtained at build time and then rejected on first use because the call supplied 12 arguments while this kernel's launcher requires 13 (one slot per formal parameter, constexpr included).
conclusion.next_suggestion: Keep the persistent kernel and pass the full launcher argument list by appending each kernel formal's value after the two pointer arguments (TILES, BLOCK, and N for the tail variant), keeping the fallback to the one-tile kernel when no raw launch is available.
conclusion.debug_lesson: The NPU launcher signature is fixed-count: probe9 captured the exact call Triton makes for the persistent kernel, [gridX, gridY, gridZ, stream, func, metadata, launch_metadata, enter_hook, exit_hook, X, Y, TILES, BLOCK] = 13 arguments. Every kernel formal parameter (including tl.constexpr ones) consumes one launcher slot, so the seed's 12-argument form is only valid for its 3-formal kernel. probe8 confirmed the TypeError 'function takes exactly 13 arguments (12 given)', and replaying the 13-argument form was exact and ~51us per call with a 33.5us device time. Lesson: when reusing a cached low-level launcher, derive the argument count from the kernel signature instead of copying a call from a different kernel.
conclusion.strategy_evolution: Architecture unchanged; the remaining gap is purely the host launch path, now diagnosed exactly and fixable by matching the launcher argument count to the kernel signature.

plan.strategy: Replace one-tile-per-program launches for large contiguous inputs with a persistent multi-tile kernel whose program count is the device vector-core count
plan.code_changes: Added _fix_loop / _fix_loop_tail persistent kernels (compile-time TILES/N, stride by tl.num_programs(0), num_stages=2). For n >= 8*8192 the launch uses grid = min(tiles, vector_core_num from torch.npu.get_device_properties, task-derived fallback) with BLOCK=8192 instead of one program per 8192-element tile. Small/odd shapes keep the previous one-tile-per-program paths; strided path unchanged. Launch metadata still warmed once and reused via raw launch.
plan.hypothesis: The three 4096x4096 workloads are limited by 2048 tiny single-tile programs (one serialized load->vector->store each). A persistent kernel with one program per vector core (40 on the probe device), each looping over ~51 tiles, lets the compiler pipeline the tiles and raises effective bandwidth, so fp16/bf16 speedups should roughly double and fp32 should improve slightly.

expected_effect.mechanism: Each program streams many tiles so load/compute/store pipeline across iterations instead of paying per-program dispatch and an unoverlapped single-tile DMA; measured device time for the 4096x4096 fp16 case drops from ~80us to ~34us

conclusion.root_cause: The persistent entries were built with kern.warmup(..., num_stages=2), which did not yield a usable compiled launch, so entry.launch stayed None and every call used the slow JIT dispatch path (~100us of Python per call, size independent). Additionally the threshold n>=65536 routed medium shapes (65536..1M elements, device time only a few microseconds) onto the loop path, where that fixed host cost dominated.
conclusion.perf_gap_analysis: Expected a large gain on the three 4096x4096 shapes; observed a global regression from geo_mean 0.9048 to 0.4456. Nine of twelve timing workloads moved to ~80-88us regardless of size (e.g. fix-timing-6, 1M bf16: 21.9->87.7us; fix-timing-1: 23.3->81.8us), while fix-timing-3 (fp16 16.7M) stayed flat at 80.6us and fix-timing-11 (fp32 16.7M) improved 116.6->88.7us. A size-independent ~80us floor indicates per-call host cost, not device time: the loop entry never obtained the cached raw launch (warmup with a launch-level num_stages argument failed), so every call fell through to full Triton JIT dispatch. Probe measurement of the same kernel shape put its real device time at only ~33.5us (fp16) and ~97us (fp32), confirming the device side did improve while the host path regressed.
conclusion.next_suggestion: Re-submit the persistent kernel but move loop pipelining from the launch option into tl.range(num_stages=2) inside the kernel body, warm up with the proven plain call (no num_stages kwarg) so the cached raw launch is built, and only take the persistent path when that raw launch is actually available (otherwise fall back to the seed one-tile kernel). That keeps the 33.5us device win without risking the JIT-dispatch regression.
conclusion.debug_lesson: Three probes and one eval established the mechanism: (1) the persistent loop kernel's *device* time is genuinely better (reps-slope K=33.5us fp16 16.7M vs ~80us for one-tile-per-program; probe5: constexpr vs runtime TILES identical, 33.5 vs 31.3); (2) the eval regression came from launch metadata: probe6 showed raw_launch=False for loop-path entries, so every call paid full Triton JIT dispatch (cand.run 175us vs torch.fix 80us per call in the debug harness); (3) a constexpr-vs-runtime TILES change is not a factor, so the failed warmup(..., num_stages=2) call is the suspect. Lesson: verify that the cached raw launch actually exists before assuming a kernel-structure win translates to end-to-end time.
conclusion.strategy_evolution: Architecture is right but the host launch path must be preserved: keep the persistent multi-tile kernel, move pipelining into the kernel body, and make the persistent path conditional on a successful cached raw launch with the seed kernel as fallback.

plan.strategy: Keep the persistent multi-tile kernel but guarantee its host launch path: pipelining inside the kernel body, plain warmup, and fall back to the seed kernel if no cached raw launch is obtained
plan.code_changes: Moved loop pipelining from the launch option into the kernel body (tl.range(..., num_stages=2)) and warm up the persistent kernel with the plain, already-proven call (no num_stages kwarg) so the cached raw launch is actually built. Added a plain-range kernel variant as a build-time fallback. The persistent entry is now only used when compiled.run.launch is available; otherwise the one-tile-per-program kernel is used for that shape.
plan.hypothesis: Round 2's regression was caused purely by the lost raw launch (JIT dispatch per call), not by the kernel. With pipelining baked into tl.range and a plain warmup, the persistent kernel should keep its ~33.5us device time (fp16 16.7M) end to end, lifting fix-timing-3/-7 from 0.31 to about 0.7, while medium and small shapes stay on their previous (~22us host-bound) behaviour thanks to the fallback.

expected_effect.mechanism: Same persistent kernel now runs through the cached low-level launch (~20us host) instead of Triton JIT dispatch (~100us host), so the measured 33.5us device time for fp16 16.7M is no longer masked

key_params.fallback: one-tile kernel when no raw launch

conclusion.root_cause: The cached low-level launcher call copied from the seed kernel passes 9 fixed slots plus 3 values (X, Y, BLOCK) for a 3-formal kernel. The persistent kernel has 4 formals (X, Y, TILES, BLOCK), so the launcher needs 13 arguments; the 12-argument call raised TypeError, which the fallback silently converted into permanent JIT dispatch for that shape.
conclusion.perf_gap_analysis: Expected the persistent kernel to reach about 0.7 on the fp16/bf16 4096x4096 shapes; observed all nine loop-path workloads pinned at 85-88us with geo_mean 0.4268. The measured pattern matches max(host, device) with a constant ~85us host cost: fix-timing-11 (fp32 16.7M, device ~97-106us) is unaffected at 106.3us (speedup 1.008, better than round 1's 116.6us), while fp16 16.7M (device ~33.5us) still costs 85.2us. So the device improvement is real but the host path is still Triton JIT dispatch: the cached raw launch was obtained at build time and then rejected on first use because the call supplied 12 arguments while this kernel's launcher requires 13 (one slot per formal parameter, constexpr included).
conclusion.next_suggestion: Keep the persistent kernel and pass the full launcher argument list by appending each kernel formal's value after the two pointer arguments (TILES, BLOCK, and N for the tail variant), keeping the fallback to the one-tile kernel when no raw launch is available.
conclusion.debug_lesson: The NPU launcher signature is fixed-count: probe9 captured the exact call Triton makes for the persistent kernel, [gridX, gridY, gridZ, stream, func, metadata, launch_metadata, enter_hook, exit_hook, X, Y, TILES, BLOCK] = 13 arguments. Every kernel formal parameter (including tl.constexpr ones) consumes one launcher slot, so the seed's 12-argument form is only valid for its 3-formal kernel. probe8 confirmed the TypeError 'function takes exactly 13 arguments (12 given)', and replaying the 13-argument form was exact and ~51us per call with a 33.5us device time. Lesson: when reusing a cached low-level launcher, derive the argument count from the kernel signature instead of copying a call from a different kernel.
conclusion.strategy_evolution: Architecture unchanged; the remaining gap is purely the host launch path, now diagnosed exactly and fixable by matching the launcher argument count to the kernel signature.

plan.strategy: Measure the provided seed implementation unchanged to establish the baseline latency and correctness for torch.fix truncation
plan.code_changes: None; seed written verbatim to tmp/main.py
plan.hypothesis: The seed's floor/ceil + sign-bit restoration kernel preserves -0/NaN/Inf semantics and passes all 18 correctness cases; baseline geo_mean establishes the reference ratio

conclusion.root_cause: Seed baseline passes all 18 correctness cases bit-exactly (abs_err=0, matched_ratio=1) but is slow: geo_mean 0.518. Two independent gaps, both measured: (1) per-call host cost is ~26 us versus ~14 us for the reference torch.fix on every workload with n<=1M (9 of 12 timing cases sit at a flat 0.67-0.74x regardless of size, so the difference is host submit, not device work); (2) at n=16.7M the device kernel costs ~127 us of the ~152 us latency while the reference executes the same case inside its ~19.8 us host floor, and fp16 (0.13x) and fp32 (0.13x/0.59x) cost nearly the same despite 2x different byte counts, which points to vector-instruction count and per-block overhead rather than DMA bandwidth. The seed's kernel also masks every load/store even when BLOCK divides n exactly, and spends 9 vector ops per element (cvt, cmp, floor, ceil, select, 2x and, or, cvt).
conclusion.perf_gap_analysis: No previous measurement to compare against (first round). Workload-level facts recorded for the next round: flat ~0.69x for n in {1024, 65536, 1048576} across fp16/bf16/fp32, 0.1298x for fp16 4096x4096, 0.1287x for bf16 4096x4096, 0.5876x for fp32 4096x4096; min_speedup 0.1287 at fix-timing-7.
conclusion.next_suggestion: Remove the per-element mask on the contiguous path when BLOCK divides n, raise the tile to 8192 elements, replace floor+ceil+select (9 vector ops) with an abs/floor/sign-restore form (6 vector ops), and slim the host path (drop memory_format on the fast path, cache the raw-stream getter and device index) to attack both the flat host-bound cases and the op-count-bound 16.7M cases.
conclusion.debug_lesson: Target-side probing showed torch.empty_like ~5.6 us and the raw Triton launcher dominating the remaining host cost; because eval timing is submit-limited for all n<=1M, device-side tuning cannot move those cases.
conclusion.strategy_evolution: Baseline measured; next round attacks mask removal, tile size, vector-op count and host glue together, then a final round tunes based on per-case evidence.

conclusion.debug_lesson: Three probes and one eval established the mechanism: (1) the persistent loop kernel's *device* time is genuinely better (reps-slope K=33.5us fp16 16.7M vs ~80us for one-tile-per-program; probe5: constexpr vs runtime TILES identical, 33.5 vs 31.3); (2) the eval regression came from launch metadata: probe6 showed raw_launch=False for loop-path entries, so every call paid full Triton JIT dispatch (cand.run 175us vs torch.fix 80us per call in the debug harness); (3) a constexpr-vs-runtime TILES change is not a factor, so the failed warmup(..., num_stages=2) call is the suspect. Lesson: verify that the cached raw launch actually exists before assuming a kernel-structure win translates to end-to-end time.
conclusion.strategy_evolution: Architecture is right but the host launch path must be preserved: keep the persistent multi-tile kernel, move pipelining into the kernel body, and make the persistent path conditional on a successful cached raw launch with the seed kernel as fallback.

plan.strategy: Keep the persistent multi-tile kernel but guarantee its host launch path: pipelining inside the kernel body, plain warmup, and fall back to the seed kernel if no cached raw launch is obtained
plan.code_changes: Moved loop pipelining from the launch option into the kernel body (tl.range(..., num_stages=2)) and warm up the persistent kernel with the plain, already-proven call (no num_stages kwarg) so the cached raw launch is actually built. Added a plain-range kernel variant as a build-time fallback. The persistent entry is now only used when compiled.run.launch is available; otherwise the one-tile-per-program kernel is used for that shape.
plan.hypothesis: Round 2's regression was caused purely by the lost raw launch (JIT dispatch per call), not by the kernel. With pipelining baked into tl.range and a plain warmup, the persistent kernel should keep its ~33.5us device time (fp16 16.7M) end to end, lifting fix-timing-3/-7 from 0.31 to about 0.7, while medium and small shapes stay on their previous (~22us host-bound) behaviour thanks to the fallback.

expected_effect.mechanism: Same persistent kernel now runs through the cached low-level launch (~20us host) instead of Triton JIT dispatch (~100us host), so the measured 33.5us device time for fp16 16.7M is no longer masked

key_params.fallback: one-tile kernel when no raw launch

conclusion.root_cause: The cached low-level launcher call copied from the seed kernel passes 9 fixed slots plus 3 values (X, Y, BLOCK) for a 3-formal kernel. The persistent kernel has 4 formals (X, Y, TILES, BLOCK), so the launcher needs 13 arguments; the 12-argument call raised TypeError, which the fallback silently converted into permanent JIT dispatch for that shape.
conclusion.perf_gap_analysis: Expected the persistent kernel to reach about 0.7 on the fp16/bf16 4096x4096 shapes; observed all nine loop-path workloads pinned at 85-88us with geo_mean 0.4268. The measured pattern matches max(host, device) with a constant ~85us host cost: fix-timing-11 (fp32 16.7M, device ~97-106us) is unaffected at 106.3us (speedup 1.008, better than round 1's 116.6us), while fp16 16.7M (device ~33.5us) still costs 85.2us. So the device improvement is real but the host path is still Triton JIT dispatch: the cached raw launch was obtained at build time and then rejected on first use because the call supplied 12 arguments while this kernel's launcher requires 13 (one slot per formal parameter, constexpr included).
conclusion.next_suggestion: Keep the persistent kernel and pass the full launcher argument list by appending each kernel formal's value after the two pointer arguments (TILES, BLOCK, and N for the tail variant), keeping the fallback to the one-tile kernel when no raw launch is available.
conclusion.debug_lesson: The NPU launcher signature is fixed-count: probe9 captured the exact call Triton makes for the persistent kernel, [gridX, gridY, gridZ, stream, func, metadata, launch_metadata, enter_hook, exit_hook, X, Y, TILES, BLOCK] = 13 arguments. Every kernel formal parameter (including tl.constexpr ones) consumes one launcher slot, so the seed's 12-argument form is only valid for its 3-formal kernel. probe8 confirmed the TypeError 'function takes exactly 13 arguments (12 given)', and replaying the 13-argument form was exact and ~51us per call with a 33.5us device time. Lesson: when reusing a cached low-level launcher, derive the argument count from the kernel signature instead of copying a call from a different kernel.
conclusion.strategy_evolution: Architecture unchanged; the remaining gap is purely the host launch path, now diagnosed exactly and fixable by matching the launcher argument count to the kernel signature.
